chunk-001:c004.proposition: A part is any positive ontological item intrinsic to a subject yet distinct from it, so absolute divine simplicity entails that anything intrinsic to God is identical to God.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: Aseity need not entail simplicity because dependence may be counterfactual, God may ground his own parts, strong aseity may conflict with Trinitarian multiplicity, or aseity may exclude only dependence on realities outside God.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-01.proposition: Trinitarianism and classical divine simplicity form an inconsistent tetrad if divine processions are positive ontological items intrinsic to God yet distinct from God.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-03.proposition: The Son's begottenness asymmetrically distinguishes the Son from the unbegotten Godhead, yielding a positive intrinsic item not strictly identical with God and therefore composition under the operative criterion.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-05.proposition: In a possible world where God creates nothing, God's contingent knowledge must be intrinsic, making it a contingent accident in God contrary to divine simplicity.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-01.proposition: Even if the truth corresponding to divine knowledge is extrinsic, knowledge of positive contingent truths still includes a contingent intrinsic component in God.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-02.proposition: If an omniscient God acquires and loses knowledge as contingent reality changes, then God has potentiality and classical divine simplicity is false.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-04.proposition: An account assigning differences in divine knowledge wholly to extrinsic reality must explain what God's temporally changing creature-specific knowledge consists in without emptying the concept of knowledge.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-06.proposition: God could rationally choose to create nothing because his reasons may exceed human understanding, undiluted perfection may be preferable, or divine self-sufficiency may favor existing alone.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-09.proposition: On the truthmaker account of divine simplicity, distinct true predications about God may differ in meaning while sharing God himself as their single truthmaker.
